Order No.04 Dated- 16.05.2024 Heard learned counsel for the parties.

2. Apprehending their arrest in connection with Sadar(Mahila) P.S. Case No. 04 of 2022 instituted under Sections 498A, 341, 323, 313, 354A, 504 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code, the petitioners have moved this Court for grant of privilege of anticipatory bail.
3. As per FIR, the allegation is that the marriage of informant was solemnized with the petitioner-Mohnish Verma.
After sometime of marriage, the informant's husband along with other in-laws started demanding Rs.15 lakhs as additional dowry from the informant.
Due to non-fulfillment of the aforesaid demand, she was subjected to assault and torture both mental and physical.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioners has submitted that the petitioners are innocent and have committed no offence at all rather they have been falsely implicated in this case due to matrimonial dispute between the parties.
It is further submitted that all the allegations levelled against the petitioners are found to be false and fabricated.
After completion of investigation, charge-sheet has been submitted against the petitioners.
Petitioners undertake to co-operate with the trial of the case.
Hence, the petitioners may be extended the privilege of anticipatory bail.
5. Learned Addl.P.P appearing for the State assisted by learned counsel or the informant opposes the prayer for anticipatory bail of the petitioners.

6. It appears that it is a case of matrimonial dispute between the parties and petitioners have co-operated with the investigation of the case and after completion of investigation, charge-sheet has been submitted against the petitioners, hence, this case comes within the guidelines laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation & Anr. reported in 2021(10) SCC 773.

sentences.text: Hence, without expressing any view on the merits of the case, this anticipatory bail application is disposed off.

7. Petitioner is directed to seek regular bail before concerned trial court which shall be disposed off on the same day in strict compliance of guidelines laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation & Anr. reported in 2021(10)
SCC 773.
